record.paper_title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
record.original_question: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ, with area A when n = 2 and volume |Ω| in general, and let λ₁ ≤ λ₂ ≤ ··· be the Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues. Is the scale-invariant quantity |Ω|^{2/n} λₙ₊₁ always at least the n-ball value C_n^{2/n} j_{p+1,1}², so that in particular A λ₃ ≥ (A λ₃)_disk = π j_{1,1}² in dimension 2?

evidence.quote: For Ω ⊂ ℝ² Aλ₃ ≥ (Aλ₃)|disk = πj²_{1,1}, and for Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ |Ω|^{2/n} λₙ₊₁ ≥ (|Ω|^{2/n} λₙ₊₁)|n-ball = C_n^{2/n} j²_{p+1,1}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain, and let $0<\lambda_1(\Omega)\le\lambda_2(\Omega)\le\cdots$ denote the eigenvalues of the Dirichlet Laplacian on $\Omega$, i.e. the values $\lambda$ for which there is a nontrivial $u\in H_0^1(\Omega)$ with $-\Delta u=\lambda u$ in $\Omega$ and $u=0$ on $\partial\Omega$. Write $|\Omega|$ for the Lebesgue measure of $\Omega$ (denoted $A$ in dimension $n=2$). Let $j_{\nu,1}$ denote the first positive zero of the Bessel function $J_\nu$, set $p=(n-2)/2$, and let $C_n=\pi^{n/2}/\Gamma(n/2+1)$ be the volume of the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$. The scale-invariant quantity $|\Omega|^{2/n}\lambda_{n+1}(\Omega)$ on the $n$-ball equals $C_n^{2/n} j_{p+1,1}^2$.

Prove or disprove: for every bounded domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$,
$$|\Omega|^{2/n}\,\lambda_{n+1}(\Omega)\ \ge\ C_n^{2/n}\, j_{p+1,1}^2,$$
with equality when $\Omega$ is an $n$-ball. In particular, in dimension $n=2$, is it true that $A\,\lambda_3(\Omega)\ge \pi j_{1,1}^2$, the value attained by a disk?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that the disk minimizes $\lambda_3$ among planar domains of fixed area (and that the $n$-ball minimizes $\lambda_{n+1}$ among $n$-dimensional domains of fixed volume) appears to remain open. For $\lambda_1$ the Faber-Krahn inequality is classical, and for $\lambda_2$ the Krahn-Szegő theorem gives two equal balls as the minimizer. For $\lambda_3$ only existence of an optimal domain (and connectedness in dimensions 2 and 3) is known; the conjecture that the optimizer is a single ball is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Minimization problems for eigenvalues of the Laplacian (Henrot)
status_evidence.snippet: For λ₃, only the existence of an optimal domain is known, and the fact that this domain is connected in dimension 2 and 3.
status_evidence.claim: The minimizer of λ₃ under volume constraint is conjectured but not proven to be a ball; only existence and connectedness results are known.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotic behaviour and numerical approximation of optimal eigenvalues
status_evidence.snippet: It is conjectured that the third eigenvalue of the Dirichlet Laplacian is minimized by a ball.
status_evidence.claim: The disk/ball conjecture for λ₃ is stated as an open conjecture supported by numerics.
